methods.name: list
methods.doc: Stream the jobs one session can see — its own plus every unowned job — as whole-set frames: one on open, then one after each coalesced burst of lifecycle commits. The stream has no natural end; the carrier closes it.

methods.name: follow
methods.doc: Stream one job's retained output from an absolute byte offset, then its terminal projection once settled and drained. Non-consuming: the model-facing cursor and notice state never observe these reads. The request's session is the fenced read's caller; the registry rejects a job the session cannot see and an unknown job.

methods.name: kill
methods.doc: Kill one background job on a human's behalf. The request's session is the fenced read's caller, so the job must be one that session can see: the registry's owner fence is the only access rule, and a child session's own jobs are killable from its list like any other. The kill records `cancelled by the user` as its reason; it is not one the model requested, so the owning agent still receives the completion notice, and a shell tool waiting on that job reads the reason in its own result.

JobChannel.doc: Stream label of one output chunk. `stdout` and `stderr` reach the model's consuming read; `log` marks producer narration (a workflow's phase lines) that only observers see. Consumers treat an unrecognized label like an absent one.

props.name: at
props.doc: Absolute offset of the chunk's first byte; offsets never move once assigned.

props.name: text
props.doc: Chunk text exactly as appended (possibly tail-trimmed by retention).

props.name: channel
props.doc: Stream label, when the producer supplied one.

props.name: gapBefore
props.doc: Bytes immediately before this chunk were lost, at the producer or to retention.

JobChunk.doc: One chunk of a job's output ring: absolute offset, text, channel, and loss marker.

props.name: from
props.doc: Offset the first `output` frame continues from.

props.name: next
props.doc: Offset to resume from after this frame.

props.name: lossy
props.doc: Bytes between the requested offset and `chunks` were already evicted.

JobFollowFrame.doc: Job observation stream frames: one `opened` anchor carrying the job's projection (its `output.earliest` and `output.total` at open time) and the offset the first `output` frame continues from, then coalesced `output` batches, then — once the job has settled and its ring is drained — one terminal `status` carrying the settled projection, after which the stream closes normally. Status rides the same stream as output so settlement can never race a still-open output channel.

props.name: sessionId
props.doc: Owning session for the fenced read. Omitted for an unowned job, which any caller may observe.

props.name: from
props.doc: Absolute byte offset to resume from (a prior frame's `next`). Omitted, the stream starts at the oldest retained byte.

JobFollowRequest.doc: Target of one `job.follow` stream: the job, its owning session, and an optional resume offset.

props.name: sessionId
props.doc: Session whose job list carries the job; the fenced lookup reads as it.

JobKillRequest.doc: Human-initiated cancellation of one background job visible to a session.

JobKillValue.doc: Receipt after the registry accepted the human kill request.

JobListFrame.doc: One `job.list` frame: the complete set the session can see — its own jobs plus every unowned job — after a lifecycle change. Whole-set replacement, so a reconnect's first frame is already the truth.

JobListRequest.doc: Target of one `job.list` stream: the session whose visible jobs the stream mirrors.

JobStatus.doc: Job lifecycle: `running`, optionally `stopping`, then exactly one terminal status. Producer-specific facts belong in {@link JobView.progress} and {@link JobView.detail}.

props.name: id
props.doc: The registry-issued id (`<kind>-<short-uuid>`).

props.name: kind
props.doc: The producer kind the job was registered with: a Host-registered `JobKind`, carried as an open string because a browser bundle or a Remote codec sees only the `JobKindMap` merges its own program compiles.

props.name: label
props.doc: The producer-supplied one-line label.

props.name: owner
props.doc: Owning session; absent for an unowned job, which every caller can see.

props.name: outputLimitBytes
props.doc: Producer-owned cap for complete model-facing notices and reads, in UTF-8 bytes.

props.name: status
props.doc: Current lifecycle state.

props.name: progress
props.doc: The producer's live progress line (`3/10`, the current phase); cleared at settlement.

props.name: detail
props.doc: Terminal reason (`exit code: 3`); a recorded kill reason is merged in.

props.name: startedAt
props.doc: Epoch ms when the job was registered.

props.name: finishedAt
props.doc: Epoch ms when the job settled; absent while live.

props.name: output
props.doc: The output ring's absolute coordinates and the complete-stream files behind it. `total` is the offset the next chunk starts at (0 while nothing was written); `earliest` is the oldest retained byte, greater than zero exactly when retention dropped the head. `spillPaths` lists the spill files the job's pull sources currently keep, in source order and deduplicated, and is absent while no source keeps one: it outlives any chunk, so a reader below `earliest` can still name where the bytes went.

JobView.doc: Read-only projection of one job — a fresh object per call, never live registry state. The model tools, the browser roster, and the observation stream all consume this one shape.
